paragraphs.source_en: The subsequent chronological-stylistic sequence elaborated by Muzzolini (1995a) is almost identical to Sansoni's one but using different values for respective phases. His division is based on superimpositions with all the problems mentioned by Sansoni and therefore subjective in many cases. For the Acacus, Mori (2000) distinguished an archaic phase characterised by monochrome figures and a final phase with polychrome images. Mori does not explain his chronological sequence which seems to be based on the assumption that a more simplistic image has to precede a complex one. For the Tassili, Sansoni (1994), Muzzolini (1995a) and Hachid (1998) believe that complex large polychrome figures were the earliest artistic tradition, small figures representing a later expression.

paragraphs.source_en: The assessment of the relative chronology is hampered by the fact that styles are repeated throughout the Round Head period. As noticed by Hachid (1998) and Dupuy (2008) and confirmed by the observation of hundreds of Round Head paintings during my fieldwork, it is evident that the styles cannot be arranged chronologically because in different shelters they are superimposed in different orders. This is most clearly evident at the Tan Zoumaitak site where various styles, namely white figures, white figures with a red border and red figures are superimposed in all possible orders (Fig. 3-6).
